theorem: The symplectic quadrangles W(3,q) yield a parametric CSS quantum code family [[(q+1)(q^2+1), q^2+1, q+1]]: k=q^2+1 logical qubits (Pass 224) and distance q+1 set by the isotropic lines, which are the minimum-weight logical operators. q=3 is the committed [[40,10,4]]; q=5,7 give [[156,26,6]], [[400,50,8]].
reading: The classical (X-type) code is the incidence code C with d(C)=q+1 realised by the n lines; every line lies in C but not in the doubly-even sentinel C^perp, so it is a weight-(q+1) logical operator, fixing the CSS distance at q+1. The register carries q^2+1 logicals but only tolerates ~q/2 errors: distance grows linearly while capacity grows quadratically -- a low-rate, geometrically rigid quantum memory keyed to the quadrangle order.
